name: Cutting the aśvattha with the weapon of non-attachment (BhG 15.3–5)
method_summary: The text gives the method as an image: the firmly rooted aśvattha (roots above, branches below, swollen by the guṇas, sense-objects its shoots, its roots below bound up with action) is to be cut with the strong weapon of non-attachment (asaṅga-śastra); then the place from which there is no return is to be sought, in the words 'I take refuge in that very primal person from whom the ancient activity flowed forth'. No further technique is given.
signs_of_progress: Free from pride and delusion, the fault of attachment conquered, constantly intent on what pertains to the self, desires turned away, released from the pairs of pleasure and pain — such undeluded ones go to the imperishable place (15.5).

name: Constancy in knowledge of what pertains to the self (BhG 13.12)
method_summary: Listed among the twenty dispositions called 'knowledge': constancy in knowledge of what pertains to the self (adhyātma-jñāna-nityatva), together with keeping in view the aim of the knowledge of reality (13.12). 15.5 counts those 'constantly intent on what pertains to the self' (adhyātmanitya) among those who reach the imperishable place. The text gives no further method.

name: Unswerving devotion (avyabhicāriṇī bhakti), BhG 13.11 and 14.26
method_summary: Devotion to Kṛṣṇa that does not stray, 'by a yoga with no other' (ananya-yoga), is counted among the dispositions called knowledge (13.11). Serving (sevate) Kṛṣṇa with the unswerving yoga of devotion is the means by which one goes fully beyond the three guṇas and becomes fit for becoming brahman (14.26). One who knows him as puruṣottama worships (bhajati) him with his whole being (15.19). No outward procedure is specified.
signs_of_progress: Going beyond the guṇas; fitness for becoming brahman (14.26).

name: Service of the teacher
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13.8: attendance on the teacher (ācāryopāsana) is listed among the twenty dispositions called knowledge; no procedure is given.

name: Resorting to solitude (vivikta-sthāna-sevana)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13.11: resorting to secluded places (viviktadeśa-sevitva) and lack of delight in gatherings of people are listed among the dispositions called knowledge.

name: Surrender (prapatti / śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 15.4: after the aśvattha is cut with non-attachment, the place of no return is to be sought with the words 'I take refuge (prapadye) in that very primal person from whom the ancient activity flowed forth'.

name: Reflecting on the evil of birth, death, old age, disease and pain
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13.9: seeing again and again (anudarśana) the evil (doṣa) of birth, death, old age, sickness and pain is listed among the dispositions called knowledge, with dispassion toward sense-objects and absence of the I-maker.

name: Dispassion (vairāgya)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13.9: dispassion toward the objects of the senses is listed among the dispositions called knowledge; 15.3: the aśvattha is cut with the weapon of non-attachment (asaṅga).

name: Cultivating sameness (samatva)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13.10: constant evenness of citta when the wanted or unwanted befalls is among the dispositions called knowledge; 14.24–25: the one gone beyond the guṇas is the same in pain and pleasure, toward clod, stone and gold, pleasant and unpleasant, blame and praise, honour and dishonour, friend and foe.

name: Seeing that the guṇas act: non-doership
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13.30: seeing actions done by prakṛti alone and one's self as not the doer; 14.19: beholding no agent other than the guṇas and knowing what is beyond them; 14.23: staying firm, unshaken, knowing only 'the guṇas are operating'.
signs_of_progress: Attaining Kṛṣṇa's state (14.19); not being shaken by the guṇas (14.23).

name: Seeing the Lord in all beings and bowing to all
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13.28–29: seeing the supreme lord standing the same in all beings, not perishing among the perishing; seeing the lord equally present everywhere one does not harm oneself and goes to the highest goal. (The Gītā here speaks of seeing, not of bowing.)

name: The Gītā's meditation (dhyāna-yoga, BhG 6.10–32)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13.25: some see the self in themselves by themselves through meditation (dhyāna); no technique is given here.

name: Karma-yoga: performing one's duty without attachment to the fruit
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13.25: some see the self by karma-yoga, as others by meditation or sāṃkhya-yoga.

name: Study and hearing of the Gītā
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 15.20: understanding (buddhvā) this most secret teaching one becomes wise and one who has done what is to be done.
